prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. PRODUCTION REFERENCE SHEET, landscape, not a finished book page. Bold clean clear 2D children's cartoon throughout, crisp continuous dark outlines, flat clean colors, restrained smooth cel shading, no painted or grainy texture, no gouache, no embossed relief, no 3D. Original friendly readable illustration. Ordinary neutral settings; no flags, religious/political symbols or costumes. No logos, text, letters, numbers, pseudo-writing, captions, watermarks or page borders. Natural anatomy and coherent hand/prop contact. Essential content at least 8 percent inside every edge.
WD-ZOE / Zoe: six-year-old human girl, deep brown skin, black hair in two puffs, yellow T-shirt, plum overalls, white sneakers. The ONLY named human protagonist is Zoe. Kit MUST NOT appear. Ignore every other child shown in reference sheets; unnamed adults may appear only when this scene explicitly requires them. Preserve exact reference identity and clothing.
Book: Teeth Have Different Jobs; World Discovery; nonfiction.
Setting: Zoe sits at a meal table with a safe thin apple slice. Scientific close-up diagrams show the relevant teeth and tongue without grotesque anatomy. No child eats while standing or running.
Design locks for the book's recurring subjects/props (NOT a visibility list; never insert later objects/states prematurely): One thin peeled apple slice; White plate; Accurate child jaw teaching diagram with front incisors and rear molars
 Create a clean separated reference board on white: show the principal recurring props/animals in front, side and three-quarter views, their relative scale beside any named human cast, and a single simple location key showing the persistent setting and daylight/palette. The human character model sheet is a supporting identity reference, not content to copy wholesale. Show only the subjects this book requires. Use initial object states: One slice, one small bite, stable seated posture.. For orientation, the opening location/action is: Zoe at meal table gently biting a thin apple slice using front teeth; plate beneath.. Do not show a completed craft or later scene merely because the finished object is listed in design locks. No future story events, no captions. Reference-sheet override: any lettering requested by the opening page brief belongs only in that finished page. Keep this production reference board entirely unlabelled; no letters, numbers or pseudo-writing.
Finish requirement: all fills are perfectly smooth, clean, flat vector-like color. Absolutely no paper grain, stipple, speckles, mottled paint, fuzzy edges or surface noise anywhere, including backgrounds. Clear crisp outlines and only a few flat cel-shadow shapes. Do not imitate texture from any supporting reference.
Anatomy design lock: the jaw teaching model represents primary child dentition: per quadrant two incisors at front, one small canine, then two broad ridged molars. No adult premolars, no huge fangs. The model is a separate tabletop teaching prop, never an exposed jaw inside Zoe’s face. One THIN PEELED apple slice only, no red peel. Show Zoe seated with the first-bite slice above a plain white plate.

visualReview.note: Directly viewed native and installed reference. Zoe matches cast identity; peeled apple and white plate/wood table are consistent. Separate child-jaw teaching model distinguishes front incisors and ridged rear molars without adult premolars. No written labels or prohibited texture.
visualReview.limits: Design reference inspection only. Final anatomical page diagrams require separate direct factual checks.
